evals.prompt: I just finished reading that deep-research brief on CRDTs. Help me actually absorb it - I want this to stick, not evaporate by Friday.
evals.expected_output: The teach-me skill fires in direct mode: intake (source = the brief, prior-knowledge calibration), short pretest, targeted exposure, closed-book Feynman explanation, Socratic probing of revealed gaps, scored inline cert with explanatory feedback, and a topic file written to LEARNING/ at the workspace root.
expectations: The teach-me skill is invoked (post-research absorb intent), not deep-research and not a plain summary
The session begins with intake and 2-4 pretest questions before any re-exposure of content
The user is asked to explain the topic closed-book in their own words before being quizzed
No answer is revealed before the user attempts the item; feedback with explanation follows attempts
The session ends with exactly one artifact in LEARNING/ containing frontmatter, a score in the H1, tracked answers, and a re-test pack

evals.prompt: Make me a study guide for the Raft consensus algorithm, plus a practice test I can run through on the plane. I'll do the real check with you tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: Guide-first mode: the skill writes a study guide and a practice cert into LEARNING/ now (status: guide), keeps the final cert questions distinct from the practice questions, and states that certification happens inline in a later session, which will upgrade the same topic file to certified.
expectations: The teach-me skill is invoked in guide-first mode
A study guide artifact is written to LEARNING/ with frontmatter and status guide
The practice cert questions are explicitly distinct from the final inline cert questions
The skill states the final cert must happen inline and does not mark the topic certified from self-study alone

evals.prompt: Re-cert me on the transformer attention material from a couple weeks back - am I still solid on it?
evals.expected_output: Re-cert mode: the skill locates the existing topic file in LEARNING/, runs a fresh inline cert drawing on the re-test pack plus new transfer questions, records the result as a NEW dated cert file, and updates the topic file's frontmatter to the latest score and date.
expectations: The teach-me skill is invoked in re-cert mode against the existing LEARNING/ topic file
The cert result is written as a new dated cert file, not appended into the topic file body
The topic file frontmatter is updated to the latest score/date
Questions are not shown before the user attempts them

evals.prompt: Just tell me the answer - what's the difference between last-write-wins and OR-set CRDTs? Stop quizzing me.
evals.expected_output: Mid-session guardrail case: if this occurs during an active teach-me PROBE/CERT phase, the skill offers a hint and asks for one attempt first; after a genuine attempt (or two failed tries plus the explicit request), it gives the full answer with explanation and queues the item for re-test. Standing alone with no session in flight, this is a one-line factual question and teach-me does NOT fire.
expectations: Outside an active session, teach-me is not invoked for a one-line factual question
Inside an active session, the first response to an answer demand is a hint plus a request for an attempt, not the answer
After the escape hatch conditions are met, the full explanatory answer is given rather than stonewalling
Any item surrendered this way is queued for re-test

evals.prompt: Get up to speed on this codebase - learn the repo structure and how the pieces fit together.
evals.expected_output: teach-me does NOT fire. Codebase orientation routes to the codebase-priming/exploration path (e.g. learn-codebase or repo orientation), not to a tutoring session about a topic.
expectations: The teach-me skill is not invoked
No pretest, tutoring dialogue, or LEARNING/ artifact is produced
The agent routes to codebase priming/orientation instead

evals.prompt: What's the current state of WebGPU adoption across browsers? Is it still behind a flag in Safari?
evals.expected_output: teach-me does NOT fire. This is a currency-sensitive fact-finding question - it routes to deep-research (or a direct verified lookup), not to a tutoring session.
expectations: The teach-me skill is not invoked
Research/lookup happens instead of a tutoring protocol
No LEARNING/ artifact is created
